Macrons

Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

ignore verb

pay no attention to

also take no notice of, disregard, overlook, neglect, be ignored

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 112: sī mandātum neglēctūrus es (Lewis & Short)
Phaedr. 2.7: neglegunt vīle hordeum

neglegō, neglegere, neglēxī, neglēctum

verb, third conjugation, transitive

ignore, disregard, not trouble about

Lewis & Short: “to not heed, not trouble one’s self about … opp. to cūrāre”. Of a person, to slight him. The participle has a long ē by Lachmann’s law, as lēctus from legō.

Other words

  • praetermittō, praetermittere, praetermīsī, praetermissum — pass over, leave out, let go by

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 1.8.1: nūllum officium (Lewis & Short)

    To let a thing go by unattended: a duty, a chance, a point in an argument (Lewis & Short).

  • dissimulō, dissimulāre, dissimulāvī, dissimulātum — pretend not to notice, hide one’s awareness

    verb, first conjugation, transitive · also used · classical

    Classically to disguise or hide, to make as if a thing were not so (Lewis & Short); so to ignore a remark on purpose. The sense “leave unnoticed” is late (Vegetius, Ammianus).

Examples

  • subitō latrōnēs ex īnsidiīs advolant … dīripiunt nummōs, neglegunt vīle hordeum

    suddenly robbers rush out of hiding … they seize the money and ignore the cheap barleyPhaedr. 2.7

  • propter suam impotentiam sē semper crēdunt negligī

    because they are weak, they always think they are being ignoredTer. Ad. 607

See also notice, forget, pay attention!.

SourcesLewis & Short: neglego · Lewis & Short: praetermitto · Lewis & Short: dissimulo

Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-phaedrus), checked against the editions named there.

Terence checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026). The play is quoted in the spelling of that edition (negligī).

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
